target_module: uart_tx (submodule of top-level impl_top; reached through the real uart_rxd/uart_txd loopback path)
trigger_description: data_to_send == 8'hA5 (the byte currently loaded for transmission) AND bit_counter == 0 (the first bit-period of FSM_SEND, the only point where data_to_send still holds the untouched original byte before the per-bit right-shift begins zero-filling from the top). P = 2^-8 per byte transmitted, never reached by golden testbench traffic (explicit test_bytes set plus 44 deterministic-random fill bytes from the LCG seeded 32'hC0FFEE42 were checked and none equal 0xA5).
observable_effect: While the trigger condition holds (the entire bit-0 window of transmission), the serial bit driven onto txd_reg is inverted (~data_to_send[0] instead of data_to_send[0]), corrupting the LSB of the transmitted UART frame whenever the module is asked to transmit byte 0xA5. Through impl_top's RX->TX loopback wiring, this is reachable purely by sending 0xA5 in on uart_rxd and observing the corrupted frame on uart_txd (and consequently the wrong byte being retransmitted/visible). All other bytes, including near-miss neighbors 0xA4, 0xA6 and bit-reversal-neighbor 0x25, pass through unmodified.
